specAnchors.text: understand that an RNA molecule is single stranded and contains uracil (U) instead of thymine (T)

primer.text: DNA stores the plan; RNA carries the working copies. This note fixes the two headline differences — single-stranded, uracil instead of thymine — then names the three working types, mRNA, tRNA and rRNA, whose roles return in the protein synthesis note straight after this one.

modules.title: One Strand, One Swapped Base
modules.opening: RNA is the working copy of the genetic message: a single polynucleotide strand, built on ribose sugars and phosphates, carrying A, G and C like DNA but replacing thymine with uracil, and appearing in the cell as mRNA, tRNA and rRNA.
keyPoints: RNA stands for ribonucleic acid and is a polynucleotide.
Its bases are adenine, guanine, cytosine and uracil.
Uracil takes the place that thymine holds in DNA.
RNA is single-stranded, one polynucleotide chain.
mRNA, tRNA and rRNA are the taught RNA types, with mRNA the transcript copy of a gene.

low.restatement: RNA is one strand long and swaps thymine for uracil.
low.analogy: A photocopy of one page, written in slightly different ink colours.
low.examPointer: The two headline differences are single-stranded and uracil.

medium.restatement: The chain of ribose-phosphate units carries projecting bases, and the base inventory U-without-T identifies RNA instantly.
medium.analogy: A ladder with only one rail, its rungs painted in a recognisably different set of colours.
medium.examPointer: Attach a role to each RNA type when asked to name them.

glossary.definition: Ribonucleic acid, a single-stranded polynucleotide containing uracil.
A long chain of many linked nucleotides.
The base that takes thymine's place in RNA.
Messenger RNA, the transcript copy of a gene.
